channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Globo e Febraban articularam fim de limite de horas para altos salários
item.description: Globo and Febraban negotiated with the Lula government and Chamber President Hugo Motta to include in a constitutional amendment the end of the 6x1 work scale, eliminating hourly limits for those earning above R$21,800. The talks involved eight sources and aim to flexibilize working hours for high earners.

item.title: Nacionalismo às avessas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's visit to the White House was partly seen as a tactic to divert attention from his scandal involving Daniel Vorcaro, but it also served the stated purpose of urging the Trump administration to designate Brazilian criminal organizations as terrorists — a request later fulfilled by the State Department. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Definição dos EUA sobre CV e PCC serem terroristas reforça segurança como tema eleitoral, pressiona Lula e dá discurso a Flávio
item.description: The U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist groups revitalizes public security as a central theme in the 2026 Brazilian elections, increasing pressure on Lula due to his perceived weakness on crime while giving Flávio Bolsonaro political ammunition to recover from a recent scandal. Bolsonaro’s allies argue the label enables harsher penalties and financial strangling of criminal factions, aligning with Quaest’s finding that security is Brazilians’ top concern. Though Congress advances measures like reducing the age of criminal responsibility and restricting prison furloughs, the Security PEC remains stalled in the Senate without a rapporteur or vote schedule.

item.title: Proibição para aumentos, garantia de bancos e flexibilização de regras: entenda acordo para 'salvar' o BRB
item.description: The Federal District government and the federal administration of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reached an agreement to capitalize the Bank of Brasília (BRB) with a loan of up to R$ 6.5 billion from the Credit Guarantee Fund (FGC), aimed at covering losses from transactions with Banco Master. The deal, homologated by Supreme Court Minister Luiz Fux, does not make the Union a guarantor but includes backing from a syndicate of major banks. The measure seeks to stabilize BRB and prevent systemic risks in the financial system.

item.title: Entenda como a ONU diferencia “terroristas” de organizações criminosas
item.description: The UN distinguishes terrorist groups from criminal organizations based on objectives: terrorism is driven by political or ideological motives, while organized crime focuses on material profit. According to the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (Untoc), a group must have a structure of three or more people, operate over time, commit serious crimes, and seek financial gain to be classified as criminal. However, terrorist groups that use criminal methods like drug trafficking or extortion to fund their causes may fall under Untoc’s scope, affecting extradition and mutual legal assistance laws.

item.title: Pré-candidatos celebram classificação de PCC e CV como “terroristas”
item.description: Presidential pre-candidates celebrated the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, framing it as a victory against organized crime and a criticism of the Lula government, which they accuse of protecting criminal factions. Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema praised the move as an act of sovereignty and effective security policy, while Renan Santos stressed that repression should be carried out by Brazilian forces.

item.title: Lula sanciona Dia Nacional da Artesã e do Artesão
item.description: President Lula signed into law the establishment of National Artisan Day, set for March 19, and the regulation of the profession, including the creation of the National Artisan Card. The law provides for technical assistance, commercialization incentives, campaigns to valorize women's artisan work, and support for participation in fairs and exhibitions, with provisions to recognize additional crafts based on cultural, social, and economic relevance.

item.title: Governistas criticam Flávio após EUA listarem PCC e CV como “terroristas”
item.description: Government allies and Minister Guilherme Boulos (Psol) criticized Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) after the U.S. designated PCC and CV as terrorist groups, linking the move to his meeting with Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Boulos questioned whether Rio militias tied to the Bolsonaro family would also be listed, while PT deputies accused Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro of seeking U.S. support to harm Brazil. The U.S. decision was condemned as interference in national sovereignty by lawmakers across the spectrum.

item.title: Flávio explora decisão dos EUA como trunfo eleitoral, e aliados de Lula focam 'Dark Horse' e soberania
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) plans to leverage the U.S. decision on PCC and CV as an electoral trump card, comparing it to Lula’s administration and shifting focus from the 'Dark Horse' case to public security. His allies aim to reinforce the narrative that Lula is weak against organized crime. The strategy seeks to exploit law-and-order themes to gain electoral traction in 2026.

item.title: “JN” dá 12 minutos à classificação de PCC e CV como “terroristas”
item.description: TV Globo's Jornal Nacional dedicated nearly 12 minutes to covering the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, explaining the context, implementation timeline, and Brazil's opposition to the measure. The segment also addressed the legal and economic implications for Brazil and the impact on bilateral relations, particularly following a meeting between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Donald Trump, in which the senator reportedly requested the designation.

item.title: Além de CV e PCC como terroristas, aliados de Flávio pediram a Trump volta de Magnitsky a Moraes
item.description: Allies of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, businessman Paulo Figueiredo and former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro urged the U.S. government to impose sanctions on Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes under the Magnitsky Act. They labeled Moraes as part of an alleged institutional threat, equating him with criminal groups like PCC and CV, sparking political backlash. The request comes amid rising tensions between the federal government and the Judiciary.

item.title: Entenda por que o governo Lula não classifica PCC e CV como “terroristas”
item.description: The Lula government opposes the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as Foreign Terrorist Organizations, warning it could serve as a pretext for unilateral U.S. intervention in Brazil, threaten national sovereignty, and harm the Brazilian economy through sanctions on financial institutions linked to the groups, even indirectly. The move deepens existing legal divergences with Washington and is seen as a post-Venezuela invasion escalation risk.

item.title: Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública alerta para impacto de decisão e Trump sobre PCC e CV
item.description: The Brazilian Public Security Forum criticized the U.S. decision to designate PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, stating it has profound implications for Brazilian sovereignty and was captured by electoral dispute. The forum lamented that political leaders view the measure as a simplistic solution to a complex problem, stressing the need for action in areas like fintechs, betting, and cryptoassets. The U.S. decision came two days after Trump’s meeting with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who reportedly requested the measure.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio aposta que ação de Trump sobre PCC e CV deixará caso Vorcaro em segundo plano
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) pre-campaign hopes that the U.S. decision to label PCC and CV as terrorist groups will shift focus away from his ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro. The strategy aims to minimize the Vorcaro case's impact by emphasizing international security narratives.

item.title: Governo Lula diz que decisão dos EUA ganhou ‘impulso’ com visita de Flávio e teme impacto nos bancos
item.description: The Lula government is meeting to assess a response to the U.S. designation of Brazil’s PCC and CV factions as terrorist organizations, a move officials believe was politically boosted by Flávio Bolsonaro’s visit to the White House. The administration views the designation as a potential pretext for U.S. intervention and warns of economic repercussions, particularly for Brazilian banks, citing sanctions on Mexican financial institutions last year. While the Presidency or Itamaraty will decide on an official reaction, Celso Amorim has already condemned the move as unacceptable, affirming that cooperation on security is welcome but not under coercion.

item.title: Supremo precisará regular plataformização do trabalho, diz Barroso
item.description: Former STF justice Luís Roberto Barroso stated that the Supreme Court will need to regulate platform-based work due to congressional inaction, noting that digital platforms like Uber and iFood have disrupted traditional employment relationships. He argued that platform workers deserve benefits such as pensions, social security, and maximum working hours, and that judicial intervention is inevitable absent legislative consensus. The debate, initiated in 2024 with PLP 12/2024 and continued in 2025 with PLP 152/2025, remains unresolved despite a pledge by the Chamber president to vote on it by early April 2026.

item.title: Castro desiste de candidatura ao Senado após ser alvo de ações da PF
item.description: Former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro withdrew his pre-candidacy for the Federal Senate from the PP party after being targeted by Federal Police operations investigating alleged financial fraud involving over R$ 3 billion from the RioPrevidência fund invested in Banco Master, owned by Daniel Vorcaro. Castro stated his decision aims to focus on defending himself against the accusations, which he claims are unfounded, and noted that the TSE will rule on his appeal against ineligibility on June 2.

item.title: PT acusa Bolsonaro de “entregar o Brasil” a Trump
item.description: The leader of the PT in Congress, Pedro Uczai, accused Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro of colluding with the Trump administration to 'sell out Brazil' to the U.S., following the designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations by the United States. He criticized the alleged coordination between the Bolsonaros and the U.S. government, claiming it undermines national sovereignty.

item.title: Decisão de Trump sobre PCC e CV é abusiva e afronta a soberania brasileira, diz ex-ministro da Justiça
item.description: Former Justice Minister José Eduardo Cardozo criticized the Trump administration's designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, calling it abusive and an affront to Brazilian sovereignty. He argued that Brazil's legal definition of terrorism does not apply to criminal factions and warned the move could justify foreign intervention. Cardozo also rejected the Bolsonaro family's support, stating it denies the sovereignty of the Brazilian people.

item.title: As reações de bolsonaristas e governistas à decisão de Trump sobre PCC e CV
item.description: Bolsonarists celebrated Donald Trump's decision to designate Brazil's PCC and CV as global terrorist organizations, hailing it as a public security victory and validation of Flávio Bolsonaro's efforts. The Lula government is still formulating its response to the measure, announced two days after Trump's White House meeting with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. PL allies, including Eduardo Bolsonaro, Paulo Figueiredo, Rogério Marinho, and Deltan Dallagnol, praised the move as a blow against narco-terrorism and a sign of strength for the Brazilian right.

item.title: Governo libera R$ 150 mi do Fundo Amazônia para pesquisas
item.description: The federal government announced a R$150 million investment from the Amazon Fund into the Desafios da Amazônia program, unveiled in Iranduba (AM) with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in attendance. The funding will support 18 collaborative projects focused on technological innovation in socio-production chains such as açaí, cacau, Brazil nuts, babassu, and fish, with an average of R$7 million per initiative, including research fellowships and institutional strengthening. This forms part of a broader R$7+ billion package for Amazonas, covering BR-319 roadworks, Luz Para Todos energy access, and the Manaus Moderna Terminal project.

item.title: Lula sanciona lei que cria Universidade Federal Indígena
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed into law the creation of the Federal Indigenous University (Unind), the first of its kind in the country, with activities set to begin in 2027. The institution will offer ten courses in teacher training, collective and indigenous health, territorial and environmental management, serving up to 2,800 students within four years. The initiative, developed through over 20 regional seminars with Indigenous leaders, aims to valorize traditional knowledge and strengthen Indigenous higher education.

item.title: Assessor de Lula sobre enquadramento de PCC e CV por EUA: ‘pretexto para intervenção inaceitável’
item.description: Celso Amorim, chief advisor to the Presidency, condemned the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations as an unacceptable pretext for American intervention in Brazil, while affirming that international cooperation on money laundering and arms trafficking is welcome. The announcement by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, effective June 5, comes two days after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro met with Trump and urged the designation of the groups as terrorists.

item.title: Planalto teme narrativa bolsonarista após decisão dos EUA contra facções
item.description: The Lula administration was surprised by the U.S. decision to label the Comando Vermelho and Primeiro Comando da Capital as terrorist organizations, fearing that Bolsonarist narratives will exploit the announcement to criticize the federal government on security. The Planalto team is calibrating an official response to avoid politicization while reinforcing international cooperation against organized crime and resisting opposition pressure.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro diz que PCC e CV ‘vão poder ser combatidos igual Bin Laden era’ pelos EUA
item.description: Federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro welcomed the U.S. government's designation of the PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, stating it will allow them to be combated with the same intensity used against Osama Bin Laden. He emphasized that the move will hinder the groups' financial operations and enable coordinated action between the DEA and U.S. Armed Forces in cocaine-producing countries. Bolsonaro also suggested that, by 2027, his brother Flávio Bolsonaro will be able to act more effectively on public security due to this initiative.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro celebra decisão dos EUA de classificar PCC e CV como terroristas: ‘Grande dia’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a pre-candidate for president, celebrated the U.S. decision to designate Brazil’s PCC and CV as international terrorist organizations, announced by the State Department on May 28, 2026. He said he had urged the measure during meetings with Trump at the White House and with Secretary Marco Rubio, though the U.S. government had been reviewing the issue for months. The designation takes effect on June 5, despite opposition from the Lula government, which fears it could justify extraterritorial U.S. military actions.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro tenta transformar decisão dos EUA em trunfo político, enquanto governo monitora risco de interferência externa
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is seeking to leverage the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations as a political advantage to pressure the Lula government on public security, linking the move to his agenda and his meeting with Marco Rubio. The Brazilian government views the decision as anticipated and primarily aimed at domestic U.S. audiences under Trump’s hardline narcotics policy, but is monitoring the long-term risk that it could establish a precedent for external interference in internal affairs under the guise of counterterrorism.

item.title: Por que o governo Lula era contra a classificação de PCC e CV como terroristas
item.description: The Lula government opposed the U.S. designation of Brazilian criminal factions PCC and CV as narcoterrorists, fearing it could justify foreign military intervention in Brazil. Lula argued that combating these groups is a national responsibility, citing the newly approved anti-faction law, and criticized the move as a violation of sovereignty, referencing Bolsonaro allies’ lobbying in the U.S. Minister Gleisi Hoffmann stated that terrorism has political-ideological aims and equating criminal groups with it risks enabling external interference under international law.

item.title: Nikolas dá parabéns a Flávio após EUA listarem PCC e CV como “terroristas”
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) praised Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) after the U.S. announced it would designate the PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, effective June 5. The announcement came one day after Flávio Bolsonaro met with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, sparking speculation about right-wing political influence. The Lula government warns the move could trigger automatic sanctions on Brazilian financial institutions, increasing legal and financial risks abroad due to differing definitions of terrorism between the two nations.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio vê ofensiva dos EUA contra PCC e CV como trunfo eleitoral após encontro com Trump
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign views the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations as a political asset to overcome the Daniel Vorcaro scandal and reposition the senator in the public debate, linking him to a hardline stance on organized crime and alignment with Trumpism. Led by Alexandre Oltramari and Eduardo Fischer, the strategy aims to shift focus from the Vorcaro crisis to security, international politics, and U.S. relations, leveraging the symbolic access to Trump's circle. Allies say the episode reconnects Flávio with traditional Bolsonarist voters and reinforces his image of international proximity.

item.title: Decisão do governo Trump sobre PCC e CV será munição contra Lula na eleição
item.description: The Trump administration designated Brazil's PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, a move the Bolsonaro-led opposition will exploit to attack Lula, claiming his government defends criminal groups. Lula had opposed the designation, fearing threats to national sovereignty and complications for international cooperation. Flávio Bolsonaro celebrated the decision on social media, stating he had requested the measure from Trump in a recent meeting.

item.title: 'O Brasil não aguenta mais' x risco à soberania: bolsonaristas e esquerda repercutem rótulo de CV e PCC como terroristas nos EUA
item.description: Bolsonarist lawmakers celebrated the U.S. designation of Brazilian criminal factions CV and PCC as terrorist organizations, crediting Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for his meeting with Trump and White House officials. The move is framed as a victory for public safety and a validation of hardline crime policies, while left-wing critics accuse the U.S. of violating national sovereignty and deterring foreign investment. Figures including Tarcísio de Freitas, Rogério Marinho, and Eduardo Bolsonaro praised the senator, linking the outcome to a potential 2027 presidential bid and condemning Lula’s alleged leniency toward criminals.

item.title: O “golaço” de Flávio sobre PCC e CV, segundo Nikolas
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) celebrated on social media the U.S. government's designation of PCC and CV as narcoterrorist organizations, crediting the move to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) lobbying with the Trump administration. He called it a 'golazo' by Flávio. The post was published on X on March 28.

item.title: Escala 6x1 produz curto-circuito entre PL e a campanha de Flávio
item.description: The proposal to replace the 6x1 work schedule with a 5x2 model — five workdays followed by two days off — backed by the Lula government and passed comfortably in the Chamber, has caused a short-circuit in Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign. Despite being from the PL, his father’s party, 83 of 97 Bolsonaro-aligned deputies voted in favor, exposing an internal rift. The initiative, with strong electoral appeal, highlights divisions between the government base and opposition on labor rights.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro comemora após EUA listarem CV e PCC como grupos terroristas: 'Grande dia'
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, celebrated the U.S. decision to designate the PCC and CV as foreign terrorist organizations, a measure he had advocated for in a meeting with Donald Trump. He called it a 'great day' for security in Brazil.

item.title: Lula diz estar 'chateado' com evasão de alunos do ProUni por dificuldades financeiras
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he was 'upset' to learn that some ProUni students drop out of higher education due to financial difficulties. He emphasized the program's role in educational inclusion and stressed the need for policies ensuring student retention in university.

item.title: Dino decide a favor de ex-correligionário e tira adversários da disputa pelo Governo de Roraima
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino granted a request from a former PC do B comrade, annulling a TRE-Roraima resolution that set a disaffiliation deadline for running in the interim gubernatorial election. The decision benefits the former ally by removing procedural barriers, while opponents are effectively excluded from the race under the prior rules.

item.title: Planalto diz que chamar PCC e CV de terrorismo é pretexto para intervenção
item.description: The Brazilian government rejected the U.S. designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations, arguing that labeling them as terrorism is a pretext for foreign intervention and that these criminal groups lack ideological motivation under Brazilian law. Presidential advisor Celso Amorim welcomed international cooperation on money laundering and arms trafficking but stressed that public security is a domestic matter and that the U.S. terrorism definition does not apply in Brazil, warning of potential extraterritorial legal and financial impacts on Brazilian institutions.

item.title: Discurso de Zema de que o objetivo é tirar o PT é o paraíso para Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Columnist Carlos Andreazza criticizes former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, a pré-candidate of the Novo party, for stating that his absolute goal is to remove the PT from power, arguing that this rhetoric weakens his candidacy as right-wing voters may prefer Flávio Bolsonaro, who leads in polls. Andreazza notes that this anti-PT framing anticipates a potential second-round matchup between Zema and Bolsonaro, explaining why Bolsonaro has not lost ground despite the Vorcaro scandal, and asserts that Zema would not receive bolsonarist support in such a scenario.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro comemora decisão dos EUA sobre PCC e CV
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) celebrated the U.S. government's decision to designate the PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, calling it a 'great day'. The measure was announced by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, one day after the senator met with him. The post was originally published on O Antagonista.

item.title: Metade do Senado assina “PEC do horário flexível”
item.description: The 'flexible working hours' PEC, signed by 40 of 81 senators (nearly half the Senate), allows employers and employees to choose a contract model based on actual hours worked, with pay and benefits (FGTS, vacation, 13th salary) calculated proportionally and individual contracts overriding collective agreements. Proposed by Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), coordinator of Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL) presidential campaign, it serves as a counterpoint to the Chamber’s PEC ending the 6x1 work schedule. The rapporteur for the 6x1 PEC, still undefined, will also analyze this flexible hours proposal due to thematic similarities.

item.title: Barroso declara voto em pré-candidato do PSB ao Senado no Rio
item.description: Former Supreme Court president Luís Roberto Barroso declared his support for PSB Senate pre-candidate Alessandro Molon in Rio de Janeiro during the Brasília Tech Summit. The endorsement follows the withdrawal of former governor Cláudio Castro (PL), who was leading in polls but stepped down amid a PF investigation linking him to the Master Bank case. Barroso noted he can now publicly endorse a candidate since leaving the STF.

item.title: Alcance do PCC e Comando Vermelho se estende aos EUA, diz Marco Rubio
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio designated Brazil's PCC and Comando Vermelho as foreign terrorist organizations, citing their operations extending into U.S. territory. The announcement came two days after Flávio Bolsonaro met with Donald Trump, who reportedly requested the move. The Lula government opposes the decision, warning of foreign interference in Brazil.

item.title: Amorim critica decisão dos EUA de classificarem CV e PCC como terroristas: 'Pretexto para intervenção é inaceitável'
item.description: Celso Amorim, the Presidency's advisor on international affairs, criticized the U.S. decision to designate the Comando Vermelho and PCC as terrorist organizations, stating that while cooperation is welcome, using this as a pretext for intervention is unacceptable. He stressed that public security is fundamental for socio-economic development and that combating organized crime must respect national sovereignty.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro agradece governo dos EUA após classificação de PCC e CV como terroristas
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro thanked the U.S. government for designating Brazil's PCC and CV criminal factions as narcoterrorists, stating they could now be fought like Osama Bin Laden. His remarks came in a social media video following a meeting between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Donald Trump, arranged by Eduardo and Paulo Figueiredo. Experts warn the designation could harm police cooperation between Brazil and the U.S.

item.title: Pedido de Flávio Bolsonaro a Trump contra facções pode virar ‘pauta bumerangue’
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro urged the U.S. to designate PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist groups, a move that could backfire on his campaign and harm key allies like Faria Lima. Announced by Trump two days after the senator’s White House visit, the policy imposes compliance costs and sanction risks on Brazilian banks and firms, even for involuntary or minor transactions with these groups.

item.title: Governo Lula calcula tom de reação aos EUA sobre definição de PCC e CV como terroristas por temer que soe como ‘proteção a bandidos’
item.description: The Lula administration is carefully calibrating its response to the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, fearing that a strong reaction could be seen as defending criminals, especially as Lula has hardened his rhetoric against organized crime. The primary concern is the potential threat to national sovereignty and the unpredictable legal and diplomatic consequences of the move, even while welcoming international cooperation. Advisor Celso Amorim criticized the decision as a pretext for intervention, as the government seeks to balance criticism of the designation with maintaining diplomatic ties with the U.S.

item.title: TSE marca para 2 de junho julgamento de recurso de Claudio Castro
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has scheduled June 2 for the ruling on the appeal of former Rio de Janeiro governor Claudio Castro against his disqualification from office until 2030. Castro resigned on March 31 to meet the incompatibility period for a potential Senate run, a move seen as an attempt to influence whether the temporary governor's mandate will be filled by direct or indirect election. The STF is awaiting the TSE's decision to determine if the vacancy will be filled by popular vote or legislative appointment, given the absence of a vice-governor since Thiago Pampolha left office in 2025.

item.title: Assessor de Lula diz que segurança é tema 'nacional' e que 'pretexto para intervenção é inaceitável'
item.description: Celso Amorim, special advisor to President Lula, stated that while combating organized crime is essential, labeling it as terrorism is unhelpful and using it as a pretext for foreign intervention is unacceptable. He emphasized that public security is a national matter, welcomed international cooperation on money laundering and arms trafficking, and affirmed Brazil's commitment to strengthening defense capabilities and multilateral rules.

item.title: O dia em que Trump chamou PCC e CV de terroristas
item.description: The Donald Trump administration designated the Red Command (CV) and the First Capital Command (PCC) as terrorist organizations on Thursday, March 28, just days after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) brought the issue to the White House and the U.S. State Department. The announcement followed a meeting between Bolsonaro and Trump on Tuesday, March 26.
